title.narrative: Supporting a Talent Partnership with Bangladesh

description.narrative: The Action aims to promote mutually beneficial regular and safe migration and mobility pathway and contribute to the prevention of irregular migration, by facilitating legal labour migration and mobility towards the EU. The Talent Partnership with Bangladesh was launched during the mission of Commissioner Johansson to Dhaka in November 2022, and its main components and sectors/professions of focus were endorsed during the Talent Partnership Roundtable of 1 March 2023 and 5 March 2024. Italy, Greece and Germany are the first EU Member States (EU MS) to participate in the Partnership while Romania remains as observer country.

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries benefitted from successful labour integration of the Talent Partnership programme

description.narrative: This indicator measures the total number of Bangladeshi individuals who, through participation in the Talent Partnership program, have successfully secured employment. Success is defined as the migrant workers being formally integrated into the labour market, receiving decent work as per international labour standards, and benefiting from fair wages, safe working conditions, and social protections.The indicator will also monitor the number of Bangladeshi labour migrants placed in EU Member States in sectors such as construction, healthcare, ICT, logistics, and other relevant sectors. It tracks individuals who have undergone skills training aligned with EU job market needs and have been placed in these key sectors. Additionally, it measures sustained employment, defined as workers being employed for a period of 6 months or more in the destination country during the projects timeline.This indicator only counts those who have successfully been employed through the Talent Partnership, excluding those who received training but did not secure employment
